subject: Unit economics KPI definitions (blended $/1M output tokens) + weekly reporting timeline
related_links: Confluence (draft): ADR - blended cost per 1M output tokens (pending)
Slack: #finance (thread on blended definition, reconciliation tolerance)
body:
From: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwoodinference.com>
To: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwoodinference.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: 
Date: Fri, Jan 17, 2025 at 8:12 AM PST
Subject: Unit economics KPI definitions (blended $/1M output tokens) + weekly reporting timeline

Rishi / Marissa —

Following up from yesterday’s check-in: we need to lock the KPI definition for “blended cost” so we can (1) standardize weekly reporting and (2) avoid Finance vs Product using different numbers in decisions.

My proposal is we align today on:
1) Canonical formula + inclusions/exclusions
2) “Gross” vs “net” views (discounts/credits)
3) Timeline for weekly adoption (starting next week vs after MVP dashboard)

I attached a working spreadsheet with the draft definition and a couple of examples.

Attachment: UnitEcon_KPI_Definitions_v0.3.xlsx

Key questions I need answered before EOD:
- Is the denominator strictly OUTPUT tokens? (I’m leaning yes: output tokens map more directly to GPU time, and it’s what pricing is anchored to.)
- Do we include cache effects in “blended cost” (i.e., reflect realized compute savings from cache hits)?
- For discounts/credits: can we agree to publish both a “COGS-only” view and a “net margin” view, but make the default the one Finance uses for gross margin reporting?

If helpful, here’s the strawman definition:

Blended cost ($/1M output tokens) = (Compute + Inference overhead + Allocated shared platform overhead +/- adjustments) / (Total output tokens)

Where:
- Compute = GPU fleet costs attributable to inference (on-demand + reserved amortization) allocated to requests.
- Inference overhead = serving/runtime overhead directly tied to inference workloads (e.g., load balancers, egress within serving path, VPC/NAT, etc.).
- Allocated shared platform overhead = control plane + logging/metrics storage + baseline ops costs allocated by token volume.
- Adjustments = backfill corrections / late-arriving metering corrections.

What we do NOT include:
- R&D/Model onboarding, GTM, general G&A.

Re: weekly reporting: I want FP&A to publish a simple weekly rollup (company-wide and by tier) starting the week of Jan 27. Product can follow with the richer dashboard slices once Console ships.

Laura
—
Laura Bennett
CFO, Redwood Inference



From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwoodinference.com>
To: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Fri, Jan 17, 2025 at 9:03 AM PST
Subject: Re: Unit economics KPI definitions (blended $/1M output tokens) + weekly reporting timeline

Thanks Laura — reviewed the spreadsheet.

Agree on OUTPUT tokens as the denominator for the headline KPI. Two notes:

1) We should be explicit about “output tokens” definition (metered tokens post-filtering, i.e., model_output_tokens from metering events, excluding retries that are not billed?). If Engineering only has “generated tokens” pre-finalization in some paths, we need to decide what counts.

2) For Finance reporting (gross margin), we need a stable mapping to COGS. That means:
- Compute should include reserved commitment amortization, not just on-demand.
- Any “platform overhead” allocation should be defined as a fixed pool per month with a clear allocator (tokens is okay, but it should be consistent across tiers/regions).

On credits/discounts: I strongly prefer two separate concepts:
A) Cost KPI = COGS per 1M output tokens (no discounts/credits; these are revenue-side)
B) Margin KPI = Net revenue per 1M output tokens (after discounts/credits) and/or gross margin %

If we combine credits into the cost numerator, it will confuse everyone and won’t tie out to our financials.

Cache effects: I think “blended cost” should reflect realized compute costs, which inherently reflect cache savings IF the compute allocation is based on actual GPU time or GPU-hours. But we should avoid “synthetic” adjustments like “estimated savings” in the main KPI. We can show “cache savings estimate” as a driver panel.

Re: weekly timeline: fine to start week of Jan 27 with a version that is (a) stable and (b) has an explicit “last 48h excluded due to late events” note. I’d rather have a consistent week-over-week number than a highly volatile number.

Rishi

—
Rishi Malhotra
FP&A, Redwood Inference



From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>
To: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwoodinference.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Fri, Jan 17, 2025 at 10:18 AM PST
Subject: Re: Unit economics KPI definitions (blended $/1M output tokens) + weekly reporting timeline

+1 to separating cost vs margin metrics.

From Product side, two things we need in the definition so it’s actionable:

1) It must be sliceable by model / region / tier without changing the math. I’d like the canonical KPI to be:
- daily blended cost per 1M output tokens
- at grain: date x model_variant x region x tier

2) It needs to reflect “real” cost changes when we ship runtime levers (batching, caching, quant). Agree with Rishi that the main KPI should be based on realized costs (not a savings estimate). But we DO want cache hit-rate and quantization_profile to show up as driver dimensions.

Questions / potential gotchas:
- Egress: can we clarify what counts as inference overhead vs shared overhead? E.g., streaming responses traffic; cross-AZ; telemetry export. We should keep the first definition simple and auditable.
- Retries: when we have server-side retries/fallbacks, some are invisible to customers but real cost. If those costs are material, we should decide whether they live in compute attribution or as a separate “reliability overhead” line item.

On weekly reporting: we’re fine with FP&A emailing a weekly rollup starting Jan 27. For the dashboard, we’ll ship behind internal flag first; goal is Finance/Product leadership can use the dashboard as source-of-truth by mid-Feb assuming data contracts land.

Marissa

—
Marissa Cole
Product, Console & Rollouts
Redwood Inference



From: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwoodinference.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Fri, Jan 17, 2025 at 12:06 PM PST
Subject: Re: Unit economics KPI definitions (blended $/1M output tokens) + weekly reporting timeline

This is helpful. Proposing we lock the following decisions:

A) Headline KPI (Finance + Product shared):
- Blended COGS ($/1M output tokens) = Total inference COGS / Total metered output tokens
- Denominator = metered output tokens (final, billable tokens definition from metering)

B) What’s included in “Total inference COGS”:
1) Compute (GPU fleet) including reserved amortization and on-demand
2) Inference-path infra (LB, NAT/VPC, serving egress that is required for inference responses)
3) Shared platform overhead: a defined monthly pool allocated by output tokens

C) Explicit exclusions:
- revenue-side discounts and credits (tracked separately)
- R&D / onboarding / non-inference engineering
- GTM / G&A

D) Cache / quant:
- Main KPI uses realized costs (i.e., if caching reduces GPU time, it reduces compute allocation)
- Driver views include cache_hit_rate and quantization_profile adoption, plus “estimated savings” in driver panel only (non-canonical)

E) Reliability overhead / retries:
- We include them in compute allocation (actual GPU consumed). If we need a driver breakout later, we can add a “fallback_rate / retry_rate” dimension.

If you both agree, I’ll have Elliot draft the 1-pager KPI guide and we’ll ask Platform to publish an ADR with these inclusion rules.

One remaining item: tie-out tolerance. Rishi — what’s acceptable to say in the weekly email? I’m thinking we set a goal of <1.0% variance to billing at weekly aggregate (and we annotate if the week is provisional due to late partitions).

Laura



From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwoodinference.com>
To: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Fri, Jan 17, 2025 at 1:22 PM PST
Subject: Re: Unit economics KPI definitions (blended $/1M output tokens) + weekly reporting timeline

Agree with A–E.

On tie-out tolerance for weekly email:
- Weekly aggregate variance to billing/metering: target <= 0.5%, hard threshold 1.0% (if above 1.0%, the email should say “DO NOT use for decisioning; reconciliation in progress” and we open an incident-style follow-up).
- Daily can be noisier due to late events; I’d set daily target <= 1.0%, hard threshold 2.0%.

Also suggest we explicitly exclude the most recent 48 hours from the weekly rollup to reduce churn. We can show them in the dashboard as “provisional” but keep the email stable.

If you want, I can update the spreadsheet with a summary tab that matches the weekly email format.

Rishi



From: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwoodinference.com>
To: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwoodinference.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Fri, Jan 17, 2025 at 4:38 PM PST
Subject: Re: Unit economics KPI definitions (blended $/1M output tokens) + weekly reporting timeline

Locked — thank you both.

Summary of decisions (for the record):
- Canonical KPI: Blended inference COGS ($/1M metered output tokens)
- Default KPI is cost-only; discounts/credits stay revenue-side
- “Blended” includes compute + inference-path infra + allocated shared platform overhead (monthly pool allocated by output tokens)
- Cache/quant affect KPI only via realized cost; “savings estimates” are driver-only
- Reconciliation tolerance for reporting:
  - Weekly: target <=0.5%, hard threshold 1.0%
  - Daily: target <=1.0%, hard threshold 2.0%
  - Weekly rollup excludes most recent 48h; dashboard can show provisional recent days

Next steps / owners:
1) Rishi: update spreadsheet w/ weekly summary tab + send me final v0.4 by Monday AM
2) Marissa: ensure Product requirements reflect these definitions (especially the separation of cost vs revenue/credits) and that dashboard defaults match
3) Laura (me): ask Platform to publish ADR next week capturing the canonical definition + allocation method + reconciliation expectations

Goal remains: FP&A weekly email starts week of Jan 27; dashboard becomes the internal source of truth once the ADR + data contracts are signed off.

Have a good weekend.

Laura
—
Laura Bennett
CFO, Redwood Inference
